title: Best Illustrators (2026): How to Hire One for Your Project
description: How to hire an illustrator: what the package should include, how to brief the artwork, what drives the price, usage rights and red flags.
intro: Illustration gives a brand, book, website or product a look nobody else has. Because every illustrator has a personal style, the most important choice is finding one whose portfolio already looks like what you want. Projects go wrong when usage rights are unclear, the style drifts from the samples, or AI-generated work is sold as hand-made. This guide covers what to check.

faq.q: How do I choose an illustrator?
faq.a: By style first. Look for several finished pieces in the portfolio that match the look you want. Asking an illustrator to work far outside their usual style rarely gives the best result.

It varies. Some illustrators transfer full rights; others grant a license for specific uses, such as a book cover or website, with extra fees for products or ads. Agree on the exact uses in writing before work starts.

faq.q: Which file formats should I ask for?
faq.a: High-resolution files for print, web-ready files for screens, and vector files if the art will be resized a lot, such as for logos or merchandise. Ask whether a layered source file is included.

Ask directly. Some use AI tools in their process, others do not. If you need original, copyright-clear art, for example for a trademark or product, confirm that the work is made by hand or with tools that give you clear rights.
Most packages include revisions at the sketch stage and a few small changes at the final stage. Big changes after coloring usually cost extra, so approve the sketch carefully.
